name: Primary Pulmonary Vein Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Primary Pulmonary Vein Stenosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of pulmonary vein narrowing or obstruction on imaging (echocardiography, CT angiography, or cardiac MRI)
Exclusion of secondary causes of pulmonary vein stenosis such as post-surgical or post-radiation changes
Clinical or hemodynamic evidence of pulmonary hypertension related to pulmonary vein obstruction
Presence of respiratory symptoms consistent with pulmonary venous obstruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed pulmonary vein stenosis with exclusion of secondary causes and clinical evidence of pulmonary hypertension
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary assessment including cardiology and radiology input.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive pulmonary vein narrowing detected on imaging
searchTerms: narrowing of lung veins seen on imaging
failure to gain weight as expected

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating cardiac strain
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: Echocardiography showing pulmonary vein flow abnormalities and pulmonary hypertension
CT angiography or cardiac MRI demonstrating pulmonary vein stenosis and collateral vessel formation
Cardiac catheterization confirming elevated pulmonary venous pressures
genetic: No well-established genetic mutations identified; idiopathic in most cases
other: Histopathology may show intimal proliferation and fibrosis in pulmonary veins

distinguishingFeatures: History of cardiac surgery or radiation
Localized stenosis related to surgical sites
Elevated pulmonary arterial pressures without venous obstruction

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
references: Latus H, et al. Primary pulmonary vein stenosis in children: clinical course and outcome. Eur J Pediatr. 2019.
Emani SM, et al. Pulmonary vein stenosis: diagnosis and management. Semin Thorac Cardiovasc Surg Pediatr Card Surg Annu. 2018.
